subject: FinMetrics — Dedicated capacity validation: throughput & GPU comparison (next steps)

Subject: FinMetrics post-demo recap — perf targets & dedicated validation plan

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — really helpful context on your latency targets and mixed workloads. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we all have a clear path to a dedicated-capacity validation.

Key notes from call:
- Target 95th percentile latency: 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), 300ms for streaming long responses (avg 800 tokens).
- Peak concurrent active sessions: ~320 (spiky bursts up to 450 for 10–20s windows).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~1.5M tokens/day, but bursty QPS pattern aligned with market open/close.
- Streaming is critical for your UI: low tail latency + partial token delivery is a must.

Proposed validation plan (high level):
1) Run two 48-hour experiments on our Dedicated pool: one with A100-80GB reservation, one with H100-80GB (quantized model build where applicable).
2) SLO scenarios: baseline (50 concurrent), nominal (320 concurrent), and stress (450 concurrent bursts) — measure 50/95/99 pct tail and end-to-end streaming latency.
3) Measure cost and effective throughput per GPU type, include token/unit economics and KV-cache hit projections.
4) Side-by-side qualitative check for generation quality when using int8/4 quantization (we’ll keep a small eval set you provided).

Deliverables we’ll share after the runs:
- Detailed SLO report (latency percentiles, p99 spikes, outlier analysis).
- GPU tradeoff matrix (latency vs cost vs throughput).
- Recommended reserved throughput and ops runbook (autoscale + fallback policies).

Next steps / asks:
- Priya/Samir: confirm the eval prompt set and redlines for acceptable quality (we have the initial file you emailed — can you confirm it’s the canonical set?).
- We’ll schedule the two reserved runs next week if you approve — preferred window Tuesday–Thursday for aligned engineering availability.
- Ben (cc): can you own the orchestration plan and attach the SLO matrix template?

Thanks — I’ll wait for a quick reply and we’ll lock the schedule.

Best,

Soojin Lee

Hey Samir / Priya — thanks. A quick ops-level note and what we’ll measure.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Run A: A100-80GB reserved (no quantization), baseline model.
- Run B: H100-80GB reserved with int8 quantized runtime + kernel optimizations.

Metrics we’ll capture:
- E2E latency (tts: time-to-first-token, p50/p95/p99).
- Streaming inter-token latency distribution.
- Throughput per GPU (tokens/sec) and effective concurrency until tail SLO breach.
- Memory and KV-cache hit ratio, so we can estimate effective tokens/second for your session mix.
- Cost estimate: hourly GPU delta * run duration + storage/I/O overhead.

Preliminary sizing recommendation (subject to validation):
- For nominal (320 concurrent): 12–14 H100s reserved with a small buffer for 450-burst handling (burst capacity policy).
- If cost is a strong constraint and your eval quality with int8 looks good, A100s with sharded KV-cache could be cost-effective but will likely need +30% headroom.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short summary that shows the microbenchmarks we run for each configuration and the SLO template we’ll populate.

[Attachment: redwood_gpu_eval_summary.pdf (report)]
[Attachment: proposed_mrp_schedule.csv (run schedule)]

I’ll do the orchestration and share the run links + preflight checklist by EOD Monday so we can start Tuesday morning.
